issues.failure_explanation: In OptEMA-M the EMA coefficient alpha_t = rho_t^{-1/2} depends on the current sample g_t (rho_t contains ||g_t||^2), so zeta_t is not conditionally independent of the noise term alpha_t(grad f(x_t;xi_t)-grad f(x_t)). The proof's identity E||s_t||^2 = E||alpha_t(g_t-grad f)||^2 + E||zeta_t||^2 silently drops the cross term 2E<zeta_t, alpha_t nu_t>, which is generally nonzero because alpha_t is a nonlinear function of ||g_t||. The stated inequality is false: take f(x)=1/2||x||^2-e_1^T x (smooth, lower-bounded), x_1=0 (so s_0 = e_1), noise nu_1 = +-11 e_1 with prob. 1/2 each (mean zero, second moment 121); then E||s_1||^2 = ((1+10/sqrt(101))^2 + (1-12/sqrt(145))^2)/2 ≈ 1.990 while E[(1-alpha_1)||s_0||^2 + B_1] ≈ 0.909 + 0.992 = 1.900, a violation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must re-derive the tracking-error recursion for OptEMA-M accounting for the dependence of alpha_t on the current sample (e.g., a conditional Cauchy-Schwarz argument with the extra cross term absorbed, or a redefinition of the algorithm making alpha_t predictable), and then re-establish the downstream chain through Theorem the:it:EMA:M.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed recursion for the gradient-tracking error of OptEMA-M is false, so the weighted tracking-error bound (Lemma lemma:sum:tail), the logarithmic bounds (Lemma lemma:G:bound), the aggregate bounds (Lemmas lemma:M:sum:s, lemma:M:sum:m) and the headline guarantee of Theorem the:it:EMA:M are all unsupported.
issues.title: Tracking-error recursion for OptEMA-M is false: the dropped cross term does not vanish because alpha_t depends on the current gradient
issues.why_classification: The lemma's statement itself is false (explicit counterexample), and every supported resolution requires reworking the tracking-error architecture of the OptEMA-M analysis (or changing the algorithm's update), so no comparable version of the affected claims is supported by the source.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding display bounds E[f(x_T)-f_*] by K·E[ln(e+ sum_t ||g_t||^2)] with a path-dependent random variable inside the logarithm. The closure step replaces this random variable pathwise by 4T(sigma^2 + L max_t f-hat_t), which requires pathwise bounds on both sum_t ||nu_t||^2 (only an expectation bound T sigma^2 via Jensen is available) and on max_t f-hat_t; it further replaces E[max_t f-hat_t] by max_t E[f-hat_t] when defining the deterministic sequence A_t. Both substitutions are invalid inferences (E[max_t X_t] is not bounded by max_t E[X_t] without an extra factor up to T, and the noise sum is bounded by T sigma^2 only in expectation). Lemma lemma:log:up is therefore applied outside its hypothesis, and the logarithmic bounds E[f(x_t)-f*] <= C_f ln(e+t) and E||g_t||^2 <= C_g ln(e+t) are not established.
